items.item: `Sources/Color Standard/Color.swift`: equality compares the stored XYZ including its white point, so
items.reason: Color.init(_xyz:_alpha:) adapts to D65 (Bradford), so every stored XYZ is D65 and equality compares one white point. Tests (in cab5b1cccfd9c886ab9cd17c8cfc369c6e3bee1b, Canonical Tests.swift) pin that a LAB color is stored under D65 and that the same XYZ given under D50 and pre-adapted to D65 is equal and hashes alike. Equality stays exact, so conversion rounding can still separate colours (README says so).

items.item: `Sources/Color Standard/Color.swift`: alpha is dropped by every conversion to or from another space
items.reason: Made the drop visible: converted(to:) documents it, and new Color.convertedWithAlpha(to:) -> (value: Target, alpha: Double) returns the alpha beside the value (named differently from converted(to:) so existing calls don't become ambiguous). Tests pin the drop through LAB, the kept alpha, and that Color->Color keeps alpha. README law updated.

items.item: `Sources/Theme/Theme.Product.swift`: `init(values:)` traps unless the array has exactly two elements
items.reason: Earlier agent's commit 1445168 (the only issue commit in 19e6be9..1445168; 19e6be9 itself is a formatting commit for coenttb/work#242): Theme is a two-case enum, so no other theme exists and the Product subscript can't trap; Theme.Product.init(values:) removed. Theme.init(_unchecked:ordinal:) stays public because Finite.Enumerable requires it; it now maps 0/1 and preconditions otherwise (an _unchecked contract, not caller input).

api_changes: New public Color.convertedWithAlpha(to:) -> (value: Target, alpha: Double)
Behaviour: Color from LAB/LCH now stores D65 XYZ (affects equality/hash and _debugRGBA, which previously misread D50 XYZ as D65)
Earlier (1445168, already on main): Theme became an enum; Theme.Product.init(values:) removed
notes: No package under repos/ uses Theme.Product(values:), Theme(_unchecked:), or relies on Color equality across white points (grep).
